problem_statement: A neighbourhood cafe is packed 7-11am but nearly empty 2-5pm; the owner wants to grow afternoon revenue without cannibalising the morning rush.
root_causes: Afternoon foot traffic is structurally low — there is no commuter flow after lunch.
The cafe is known as a morning coffee stop, not an afternoon destination.
Staff and ovens sit idle in the afternoon but still cost money.
Regulars have no habit or trigger to return later in the day.
hmw_questions: How might we give existing morning customers a reason to come back in the afternoon?
How might we turn idle afternoon capacity into a sellable product?
How might we attract a different afternoon crowd (students, remote workers, parents) without alienating regulars?
How might we make the slow hours feel like a feature rather than dead time?
triz_tradeoff: Filling the afternoon (more demand) risks straining the morning brand and quality the cafe is known for.
ifr: The afternoon fills itself with paying customers using capacity the cafe already has, at no extra staffing cost.

problem_statement: A small B2B SaaS team-scheduling tool (~400 paying teams) loses about 4% of accounts every month, mostly within the first 60 days; the founder wants to cut early churn.
root_causes: New teams never reach the 'aha' moment (a first fully-scheduled week) before the trial novelty fades.
Only the admin who signed up logs in; the rest of the team never adopts the tool.
The value is invisible — teams cannot see the time saved or the conflicts avoided.
Switching cost is low early on; a competitor is one CSV export away.
hmw_questions: How might we get a whole team active, not just the admin, in the first week?
How might we make the time-saved value visible early?
How might we raise the cost of leaving without locking people in?
How might we detect a team about to churn and intervene in time?
triz_tradeoff: Pushing adoption harder with onboarding nudges risks annoying users and accelerating the very churn you are trying to prevent.
ifr: Every new team reaches its first scheduled week on its own, and the value is obvious before the trial ends.
